coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Pier 70 Building 21 (Substation No. 5, relocated)
record.summary: A circa-1900 steel-framed, corrugated-metal-clad shop with a double-gable monitor roof (101 ft by 76 ft, 10,172 sq ft), the only surviving Risdon Iron Works building and the earliest steel-clad structure in the district, later Bethlehem's Substation No. 5. One of the three historic buildings the DDA obliges Brookfield to rehabilitate: a 66-year lease at $1 a year must be signed within a year of completing the building on Parcel E1 (Phase 2C), so no rehabilitation has begun.

notes.accuracy_caveat: REAL, surveyed building footprint (DataSF Building Footprints) as of 2026-09-17 -- high confidence in the outline itself and its match to Building 21: position matches multiple independent prose sources (adjacent to Building 12, fronting Slipways Commons) and its combined size (734.96 sq m) is within 4.4% of the previously-cited 101ft x 75ft (~703.7 sq m) documented footprint. The match rests on position, size, and satellite corroboration, not an explicit building-number tag in the footprint dataset itself (no such attribute exists there). A small 49 sq m footprint ~9m away was not included -- see digitization_method. Superseded history: STATUS CORRECTED 2026-09-13 -- this building's rehabilitation has not started as of the most recent primary sources found (see regulatory_context).
notes.digitized_from: DataSF Building Footprints dataset (real, surveyed building outlines; not tied to an Assessor parcel), cross-confirmed against ESRI World Imagery satellite tiles. SUPERSEDED 2026-09-17 a long chain of diagram/prose-based approximations (kept below for history) -- see digitization_method. Originally three converging real-world sources: (1) 2011 Port RFI "Pier 70 Preferred Master Plan" map (sfport.com/sites/default/files/FileCenter/Documents/939-Pier70_RFI_3-2-11_web.pdf, p.7/11), a scaled map with real street labels (Illinois St, 20th St) showing Building 21 immediately adjacent to Building 12 near the historic core, annotated "BUILDING 21 PROPOSED TO BE RELOCATED"; (2) Aug 3 2017 Port Commission memo (sfport.com/sites/default/files/Commission/Item%2011A%20Pier%2070%20Final.pdf, Exhibit F p.68): "Building 21 (Substation No. 5)... would be relocated approximately 75 feet to the southeast, and in its new location it would front Slipways Commons... sits directly next to the proposed new waterfront arts facility"; (3) D4D Figure 3.6.1 "Illustrative Slipways Commons Plan" (p.56/PDF p.72), a scaled plan with a real 0-50-100ft bar and "MARYLAND ST" label, captioned "the historic node of Buildings 2, 12, and 21."
notes.why_no_real_parcel: This structure has no street address in DataSF's Assessor roll and sits on the same huge, largely-unsubdivided Assessor lot (blklot 4052001) as Building 14 and other structures across central Pier 70 -- no distinct blklot exists to join for Building 21 specifically, so this feature uses the real building footprint instead, matched individually (see digitization_method).
notes.regulatory_context: Building 21, originally Substation No. 5, was relocated on-site and is one of three historic structures (with Buildings 2 and 12) the Pier 70 Design for Development commits to rehabilitating per the Secretary of the Interior's Standards (Pier 70 D4D S6.6.1). CORRECTED 2026-09-13: an earlier version of this row marked it "complete," inferred (not directly cited) from Building 21 being grouped in the D4D's rehabilitation commitment alongside Buildings 2 and 12. A follow-up research pass found the Port's own 28-acre site page (sfport.com/projects-programs/pier-70-28-acre-site) describes Building 21's rehabilitation as still to come -- the page shows a rendering, not a photo, captioned "Rendering of Pier 70 Building 21," under a "Rehabilitation of three historic buildings" heading, implying a future vision rather than a completed project. This is corroborated negatively by the Port's own June 2025 project-update deck (sfport.com/sites/default/files/2025-06/Pier%2070%20Update%20-%20June%202025%20v3.pdf), which documents Building 12 and Building 15's full rehabilitation histories in detail but never mentions Building 21 having been touched. Status corrected from complete to existing (see status.csv for this value's definition) -- a standing historic structure, not yet rehabbed, with no confirmed construction timeline.

facts.value: circa 1900 (documentary record has contradictions; a turn-of-the-century photograph shows a similar Risdon building)
101 ft 2 in by 75 ft 6 in by 44 ft high (NRHP); 101 ft by 75 ft, 44 ft in D4D Figure 6.5.4
Two-story steel frame with corrugated metal cladding, double-gable roof with wide monitors; interior divided by board-formed concrete walls
Only extant Risdon Iron Works building and earliest steel-clad construction at the Union Iron Works; associated with the yard's power distribution
Substation for the area and Port electrical storage, with a radio tower control room (as of the 2013-14 nomination)
Secretary of the Interior's Standards for Rehabilitation; the D4D lists it as 'Building 21 Substation No. 5 (relocated)'
66 years at $1/year base rent, participation rent from year 31, with sale and refinancing participation for the Port
Phase 2C with Parcels E1 and E4 (Port's proposed 2026 phasing plan)
Minimum 20 ft setback from Building 21 for adjacent new construction; its southern face may activate Slipways Commons with cafe terraces (D4D)
SF YIMBY's summary of the 2021 filing gives ~115,000 gsf of retail and arts space 'from rehabilitation' of Building 21, an implausible figure for a 10,172 sq ft building

open_questions: 'Relocated': the D4D labels Building 21 'Substation No. 5 (relocated)', but the NRHP nomination describes it in place west of the Noonan Building and no source records a move; whether the label anticipates relocation or records one is unresolved (the geometry file uses the surveyed footprint).
The Port's 28-Acre Site page shows only a rendering of Building 21, consistent with no work having started; no lease, permit or tax-credit application was found.
SF YIMBY's ~115,000 gsf figure for Building 21 likely belongs to another line of the filing; the filing itself was not retrieved.

building21.jpg and building21_exterior.jpg are straight architectural photographs taken in 2017, not scanned drawings or plans; `kind: document` fits the schema's 'page from a source document' reading but they may read better as `before` (pre-rehabilitation condition) if the record's kind taxonomy is revisited.
